content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To make cauliflower rice, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Sauté the riced cauliflower in a large skillet (7 minutes)
Step 2. Adjust seasoning with a pinch of sea salt (30 seconds)
Step 3. Garnish with freshly chopped parsley (1 minute)
Step 4. Transfer the cooked rice to a warm serving bowl (1 minute)
Step 5. Remove the thick outer green leaves (45 seconds)
Step 6. Take the food processor out of the pantry (1 minute)
Step 7. Cut the cauliflower into medium-sized florets (4 minutes)
Step 8. Pulse the florets in 2-cup batches (3 minutes)
Step 9. Rinse the cauliflower under cold running water (1 minute)
Step 10. Prepare a clean kitchen towel for drying (30 seconds)
Step 11. Clear off the main kitchen counter workspace (5 minutes)
Step 12. Pat the florets dry to ensure they don't steam (2 minutes)
Step 13. Wash the whole head of cauliflower thoroughly (2 minutes)
Step 14. Check the pantry for olive oil and garlic (2 minutes)
Step 15. Scrape down the sides of the processor bowl (20 seconds)
Step 16. Sharpen the chef's knife (3 minutes)
Step 17. Peel two cloves of fresh garlic (1 minute)
Step 18. Plug in the stovetop burner (10 seconds)
Step 19. Measure out one tablespoon of cooking oil (30 seconds)
Step 20. Place the cutting board on the counter (15 seconds)
Step 21. Locate the cauliflower in the refrigerator (30 seconds)
Step 22. Set out a large bowl for the processed grains (1 minute)
Step 23. Trim away the tough lower woody stem (2 minutes)
Step 24. Shake off excess water from the vegetable (30 seconds)
Step 25. Heat the olive oil over medium-high heat (3 minutes)
Step 26. Assemble the food processor blade and lid (1 minute)
Step 27. Retrieve a rubber spatula from the drawer (20 seconds)
Step 28. Drain the cauliflower in a colander (2 minutes)
Step 29. Sanitize the knife after initial prep (2 minutes)
Step 30. Dry the countertop with a microfiber cloth (1 minute)
Step 31. Wipe down the food processor base (1 minute)
Step 32. Fetch the cauliflower from the crisper drawer (15 seconds)
Step 33. Insert the grating attachment into the processor (45 seconds)
Step 34. Inspect the florets for any brown spots (2 minutes)
Step 35. Pour the raw cauliflower rice into the holding bowl (45 seconds)
Step 36. Fill the sink with cool water (1 minute)
Step 37. Dispose of the cauliflower scraps in the compost (2 minutes)
Step 38. Mince the garlic finely (2 minutes)
Step 39. Ensure the processor bowl is completely dry (1 minute)
Step 40. Wash your hands with soap and warm water (40 seconds)
Step 41. Remove mail and clutter from the kitchen island (5 minutes)
Step 42. Spread the florets on a paper-towel-lined tray (3 minutes)
Step 43. Place the skillet on the heating element (15 seconds)
Step 44. Add the cauliflower rice to the hot pan (10 seconds)
Step 45. Put the leftover cauliflower in a storage bag (1 minute)
Step 46. Remove the plastic wrap from the cauliflower (20 seconds)
Step 47. Crush the garlic cloves to release oils (30 seconds)
Step 48. Check the bowl for any large un-riced chunks (1 minute)
Step 49. Secure the processor lid tightly (15 seconds)
Step 50. Clean the work area of any stray crumbs (3 minutes)
Step 51. Set the table with forks and plates (2 minutes)
Step 52. Taste the rice for desired tenderness (30 seconds)
Step 53. Pick up the cauliflower from the grocery bag (10 seconds)
Step 54. Serve the cauliflower rice immediately (1 minute)
Step 55. Sauté the minced garlic until fragrant (1 minute)
Step 56. Squeeze a fresh lemon wedge over the dish (15 seconds)
Step 57. Pour oil into the bottom of the skillet (20 seconds)
Step 58. Add a pinch of black pepper to the pan (10 seconds)
Step 59. Store the food processor back in the cabinet (2 minutes)
Step 60. Take a photo of the finished meal (1 minute)
